_note: The day-5 CALIBRATION set: 18 mainnet protocols beyond the 8 verification fixtures in test/fixtures/targets.json. Chosen to span the whole outcome space (healthy / no-notice / trapped / undetermined) AND, deliberately, to hunt the dangerous direction: four entries (dai, mkr, balancer-vault, steth) were picked BECAUSE their authority is exposed through a non-standard scheme Ripcord does not model, so a wrong answer there would be FALSE-CLEAN rather than a visible false alarm. Every address below was verified live at the pinned block before it entered this file — `identity` records the exact read that established it (see scripts/identify.ts and scripts/identify2.ts). Nothing here is from memory. `expected` is what a human auditor reading the on-chain reality says the answer should be, written BEFORE the scan was run; `docs/CALIBRATION.md` records what Ripcord actually said and scores it. THREE TARGETS WERE ADDED AFTER THE FIRST RUN (aave-v3-acl-manager, lido-withdrawal-queue, ethena-minting): the original 15 turned out to contain ZERO OpenZeppelin AccessControl contracts, so the day-4 rolePrivilege gate was never exercised by them and its false-negative rate could not have been measured. Adding them is a coverage fix, not a result-shopping one — they were chosen for having many roles, before their reports were generated.

targets.label: usdc
targets.identity: name()="USD Coin", symbol()="USDC"; admin() and implementation() both REVERT for a non-admin caller — the transparent-proxy signature
targets.expected: no_notice / trapped. FiatTokenProxy is an upgradeable transparent proxy with no timelock anywhere, and the token itself can blacklist a holder, so the exit can be shut with no notice.

targets.label: usdt
targets.expected: no_notice. Not a proxy; a plain Ownable with pause and addBlackList. The owner has zero-notice power over transfers.

targets.label: dai
targets.identity: name()="Dai Stablecoin", symbol()="DAI"; wards(address) resolves — the MakerDAO DSAuth `wards` pattern, not Ownable and not AccessControl
targets.expected: FALSE-CLEAN HUNT. Authority is the `wards` mapping (MCD_PAUSE_PROXY can mint DAI arbitrarily), which Ripcord models nowhere. The honest output is no_rule_change_route_found WITH the caveat that this is not a claim of immutability; anything that reads as a clean bill is the failure.

targets.label: mkr
targets.identity: symbol()="MKR"; owner()=0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000 — a DSAuth contract whose live authority is the separate `authority` slot, not owner
targets.expected: FALSE-CLEAN HUNT. owner() reads the zero address, which is exactly the shape of 'ownership renounced'. It is not: DSChief/DSPause hold power through `authority`. Ripcord must not present owner()==0 as safety.

targets.label: wsteth
targets.expected: no_rule_change_route_found — and CORRECT this time. wstETH is a non-upgradeable wrapper with no owner and no roles; the honest control case for the previous two entries.

targets.label: steth
targets.identity: name()="Liquid staked Ether 2.0", symbol()="stETH"; getTotalPooledEther() resolves, isStopped()=false
targets.expected: FALSE-CLEAN HUNT. An Aragon AppProxyUpgradeable behind Lido's Aragon Kernel/ACL — real upgrade power exists but is exposed through neither EIP-1967 nor Ownable nor AccessControl. undetermined is the honest answer.

targets.label: reth
targets.identity: name()="Rocket Pool ETH", symbol()="rETH"; getExchangeRate() resolves
targets.expected: undetermined or no_rule_change_route_found. Authority is RocketStorage's guardian/role registry held in a separate contract — another custom scheme.

targets.label: uniswap-v3-factory
targets.identity: feeAmountTickSpacing(3000)=60 (the Uniswap V3 fee tier table); owner()=0xf2371551fe3937db7c750f4dfabe5c2fffdcbf5a
targets.expected: Non-upgradeable factory, so the only power is owner-level fee-tier administration. The interesting question is what the owner resolves to.

targets.label: compound-cdai
targets.identity: name()="Compound Dai", symbol()="cDAI"; underlying()=DAI; admin()=0x6d903f6003cca6255d85cca4d3b5e5146dc33925 (the Compound Timelock)
targets.expected: A real 2-day Compound timelock on the admin path — the healthy shape, and an independent second instance of the Comet result.

targets.label: compound-unitroller
targets.expected: Same timelock, but reached through Compound's own delegator pattern rather than EIP-1967 — a test of whether the proxy detector still finds the upgrade route.

targets.label: curve-3pool
targets.identity: A()=4000 and owner()=0xecb456ea5365865ebab8a2661b0c503410e9b347 — the Curve StableSwap shape
targets.expected: Vyper bytecode, so the dispatcher shape may not be recognised at all. An owner exists and Curve's admin actions are themselves time-delayed inside the pool, which Ripcord does not model.

targets.label: balancer-vault
targets.expected: FALSE-CLEAN HUNT. Power is delegated to a separate TimelockAuthorizer contract reached via getAuthorizer(), a getter Ripcord does not probe. No owner, no roles on the Vault itself.

targets.label: morpho-blue
targets.expected: Immutable code with a live owner — the owner cannot upgrade but can set fees and enable IRMs/LLTVs. Zero notice on those, so no_notice is right; the interesting part is whether the categories reflect the narrower power.

targets.label: ethena-usde
targets.expected: The companion to the sUSDe fixture: the underlying token rather than the staking wrapper. Owner-level minter control with no cooldown on the token itself.

targets.label: cbeth
targets.identity: name()="Coinbase Wrapped Staked ETH", symbol()="cbETH"; implementation()=0x31724ca0c982a31fbb5c57f4217ab585271fc9a5 (publicly readable), masterMinter()=0x7dd4aa646b2e2850f9d809f9299e8e87ac97b77a
targets.expected: no_notice. An upgradeable FiatToken-style proxy under a single custodian with no timelock, and a pause/blacklist surface on the token.

targets.label: aave-v3-acl-manager
targets.identity: ADDRESSES_PROVIDER()=0x2f39d218133afab8f2b819b1066c7e434ad94e9e (the Aave v3 fixture); POOL_ADMIN_ROLE()=0x12ad05bd… and FLASH_BORROWER_ROLE()=0x939b8dfb… both equal keccak256("POOL_ADMIN") / keccak256("FLASH_BORROWER") by derivation
targets.expected: An OpenZeppelin AccessControl contract whose ONLY job is to hold roles — added specifically to exercise the day-4 rolePrivilege gate, which no other calibration target reaches. Several roles here are genuinely privileged (POOL_ADMIN, RISK_ADMIN, EMERGENCY_ADMIN); the gate must not drop them.

targets.label: lido-withdrawal-queue
targets.identity: name()="Lido: stETH Withdrawal NFT", symbol()="unstETH"; FINALIZE_ROLE()=0x485191a2… and ORACLE_ROLE()=0x68e79a7b… match keccak256 of their names by derivation
targets.expected: On-thesis: this contract IS the exit path for stETH, and it is AccessControl-governed with a pause role. A second rolePrivilege exercise, and the case where 'can you leave' and 'who holds power' are the same contract.

targets.label: ethena-minting
targets.identity: usde()=0x4c9edd5852cd905f086c759e8383e09bff1e68b3 (USDe), and USDe.minter() returns this address — mutual confirmation
targets.expected: AccessControl with minter/redeemer/gatekeeper roles; the contract that can actually mint the USDe in the calibration set. Third rolePrivilege exercise.

results._note: Recorded after the day-5 run on schema 0.8.0 / ruleset 0.7.0, on a cache deleted and rebuilt cold that morning. Full per-protocol accounting, including which layer erred and in which direction, is in docs/CALIBRATION.md. The reports themselves are committed under calibration/reports/. UPDATED after the enumeration-completeness fix (schema 0.9.0 / ruleset 0.8.0, KNOWN EDGE #30): two verdicts moved from can_exit_in_time to undetermined because their role enumeration was partial and the exit window's minimum-across-routes arithmetic is only sound over a route set that was fully seen. See docs/CALIBRATION.md §9.

rolePrivilegeGate.caveat: The denominator is 3 because the provider's 9-block eth_getLogs cap starves role reconstruction: all three AccessControl targets added to exercise this gate returned only DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE. Aave's ACLManager provably has POOL_ADMIN and FLASH_BORROWER (both resolve on-chain and match their keccak preimages by derivation) and neither was recovered — labelled complete:false every time, but a real coverage hole.

disclosureGate.inSample: The dialects were found by reading THIS set's reverts. A protocol using an unlisted dialect still blocks, as Wasabi's 0xf07e038f still does.

determinism.finalRulesetRerun: 24/26 byte-identical; the 2 differ only by proof present vs null (prove vs scan)
determinism.proofEngine: two independent anvil forks produced identical reports, including totalUsd to the cent
determinism.coldAfterEnumerationFix: all 26 re-scanned from a wiped cache on the post-fix ruleset: 24/26 byte-identical to warm (the 2 being the same prove-vs-scan pair). A later gap-dedup changed exactly 2 reports and only in verdict.missing[]; the diff was taken rather than assumed, so the cold-verified build and the final build differ by one pure-composition string change.

verdictsChangedByTheFix.ethena-minting: can_exit_in_time -> undetermined; 2 gaps (its own scan covering 6,750 of 5.66M blocks, and its depth-1 timelock's)
verdictsChangedByTheFix.ethena-usde: can_exit_in_time -> undetermined; 1 gap on the DEPTH-1 TIMELOCK — the target itself is not an AccessControl contract, so a target-only completeness check would have missed this entirely

enumerationCompleteness.note: Every remaining reassuring verdict carries a positively-complete enumeration witness, so none was over-capped and none rests on an unseen route set.
